items.title: How Researchers Test AI for Hidden Goals — Apollo Research
items.summary:
Can an AI do the right thing for the wrong reason? Tim Scarfe speaks with Apollo Research’s Alexander Meinke, Axel Højmark and Jérémy Scheurer about Measuring Reward-Seeking via Contrastive Belief Updates, their new research with OpenAI.

The panel asks how models infer what graders reward, why good behaviour can come from the wrong reason, and whether that difference can be measured. The conversation moves through promise-breaking, grader awareness, reward hacking, scheming, opaque reasoning and corrigibility, then turns to a detailed walkthrough of the contrastive-belief method and what its results do and do not show. The o3 results discussed here concern an intermediate checkpoint without safety training.

This episode was made in partnership with Apollo Research. MLST retained full editorial control.

items.title: Deepseek Just Did it Again!
items.summary:
DeepSeek V4 Flash (Official) Runs Locally: Benchmarks, Cost, and DGX Spark Setup

I test the official DeepSeek V4 Flash (July 31 edition) running entirely locally and break down DeepSeek’s released benchmarks, where it beats the prior V4 Pro/Flash preview and even outperforms larger models like GLM 5.2, while approaching Opus 4.8 for a fraction of the size. I also explain why benchmark harnesses matter (including DeepSeek’s agent harness and an OpenAI harness example) and highlight internal DS Bench results. I cover pricing (about $0.02/M input tokens and ~$0.30/M output tokens), token efficiency on the AI Index cost curve, and agentic coding results like Terminal Bench. Then I demo Open Code harness runs (Pokémon encyclopedia and an International Space Center tracker), show ~20–30 tok/s on two DGX Sparks in FP4, discuss the 1M context window, hardware/VRAM needs for 4-bit and 3-bit, and options like Dwarf Star for SSD offloading and mixed precision.

Thanks to @NVIDIADeveloper for DGX Sparks.

items.title: India-Japan Deal Will Move 500,000 Workers in 5 Years
